# The Portal header never marks the open section with aria-current

Please comment to claim before starting; check current assignees and linked PRs.

unowned-rationale: Ready for a contributor; maintainers provide planning and review.

## Context

The Portal's header (the logo link, Learn, News, Examples, Connect) shows which section is open by drawing a highlight on a canvas behind the links. Nothing in the DOM says so: measured headless on neomjs.com at 1440 × 900 on 2026-11-19, none of the header's links carries `aria-current` on `/`, `/learn`, `/news`, `/examples` or `/services`. A screen reader announces the same five links on every page.

## The Problem

A sighted visitor sees where they are from the highlight; a screen-reader user who lands on a page or switches sections gets no such cue from the navigation. The Portal already states the open destination in its secondary navigation (the examples group index), but not in its main one.

## The Architectural Reality

Design authority: the Portal's navigation contract in `apps/portal/view/examples/GroupIndex.mjs:16-17`: "the open destination's link (or `"All examples"` when on `/examples`) carries `aria-current="page"`."

- The header links are `route` buttons (`apps/portal/view/HeaderToolbar.mjs`). A non-editing `route` renders the button root as an `<a>` (`Neo.button.Base#updateTag` in `src/button/Base.mjs`).
- `Portal.view.ViewportController#updateHeaderToolbar` (`apps/portal/view/ViewportController.mjs:417-425`) decides the open section: it maps `activeIndex` to one of five button references and sets `headerCanvas.activeId` to that button's id. The two routes without a header link (`/about-us`, `/docs`: index 5 and 6) set `null`.
- `Neo.app.header.Canvas` (`src/app/header/Canvas.mjs`) owns `activeId_` and forwards it to its renderer in a SharedWorker. That highlight is invisible to assistive technology.
- `Neo.app.header.Toolbar` (`src/app/header/Toolbar.mjs`) adds the canvas as its `header-canvas` child. The Portal is its only consumer.
- Precedent for a component stating its state through ARIA on its own VDOM: `Neo.tab.header.Button#afterSetPressed` writes `aria-selected` (`src/tab/header/Button.mjs`).

## The Fix

Let the header toolbar own which link is open and project it twice: the canvas highlight it drives today, and `aria-current="page"` on the link.

- `src/app/header/Toolbar.mjs`: add a reactive `activeId_` config (default `null`). `afterSetActiveId(value, oldValue)` sets `'aria-current': 'page'` on the root of the button whose id is `value`, removes it from the button whose id is `oldValue`, updates both, and passes `value` on to the `header-canvas` reference's `activeId`.
- `apps/portal/view/Viewport.mjs`: give the header toolbar item a `reference` (for example `header-toolbar`).
- `apps/portal/view/ViewportController.mjs#updateHeaderToolbar`: set the toolbar's `activeId` instead of the canvas's, so the toolbar is the only writer.

## Contract Ledger

| Target Surface | Source of Authority | Proposed Behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Neo.app.header.Toolbar#activeId` (new reactive config) | `Neo.app.header.Canvas#activeId`, the highlight the Portal drives today | The button with this id renders `aria-current="page"`; the previous one loses it; the canvas receives the same id | `null`: no link is marked and the highlight clears | JSDoc on the config | AC-3's unit spec |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: On `/`, `/learn`, `/news`, `/examples` and `/services`, exactly one header link carries `aria-current="page"`: the logo link, Learn, News, Examples and Connect respectively. Switching sections moves it.
- [ ] AC-2: On `/about-us`, no header link carries `aria-current`.
- [ ] AC-3: A unit spec for `Neo.app.header.Toolbar` under `test/playwright/unit/app/` pins AC-1's move and AC-2's clear on the VDOM: `npm run test-unit -- test/playwright/unit/app/`.
- [ ] AC-4: The canvas highlight still follows the open section.

## Out of Scope

- A different `aria-current` value below a section's root (for example `true` on deeper `/learn/...` pages). The group index uses `page` for its open destination, and this issue follows it.
- The header's hover effect and the social icons.
